knowledge:
- key_parameters: windowSize=Size of the sliding window for genomic tiling (typically 50000 bp because NADs are broad genomic regions) ;; step=Step size for the sliding window (typically 5000 bp) ;; backgroundPercentage=Proportion of lower ratios used for background training (e.g., 0.25 for 25%) ;; cutoffAdjPvalue=Adjusted p-value threshold for peak calling (typically 0.05) ;; countFilter=Minimum read count threshold to filter out low-coverage windows during peak calling
- alternatives: None mentioned
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing NAD-seq data (nucleolus-associated DNA vs. genomic DNA background) to map nucleolar-associated domains across the genome.
- pitfalls: Ratios of nucleolar to genomic DNA are often higher at the 5' end than the 3' end of chromosomes, which requires chromosome-specific background correction and smoothing via smoothRatiosByChromosome. Unlike ChIP-seq, cumulative percentage curves for NAD-seq do not show sharp transitions because NADs are broad regions (up to 100 kb), but clear differences between genomic and nucleolar curves should still be visible.

workflows.name: single_pair_nad_seq
workflows.intent: Identify nucleolar-associated domains (NADs) from a single pair of nucleolus-associated DNA and genomic DNA sequencing samples.
input: genomic.bam (BAM file of genomic DNA background)
workflows.stages: 1. Calculate read coverage in sliding windows using tileCount ;; 2. Compute log2 ratios of nucleolus vs genomic DNA using log2se ;; 3. Smooth ratios per chromosome using smoothRatiosByChromosome ;; 4. Assess quality using cumulativePercentage ;; 5. Call and trim peaks using trimPeaks ;; 6. Export peaks to CSV or BED format
workflows.code:
se <- tileCount(reads=file.path(path, bamFiles), genome=Mmusculus, windowSize=ws, step=step, mode = IntersectionNotStrict, dataOverSamples = FALSE)
dat <- log2se(se, nucleolusCols = "N18.subsampled.srt.bam", genomeCols ="G18.subsampled.srt.bam", transformation = "log2CPMRatio")
datList <- smoothRatiosByChromosome(dat, chr = c("chr18", "chr19"), N = 100)
cumulativePercentage(datList[["chr18"]])
peaks <- lapply(datList, trimPeaks, backgroundPercentage=backgroundPercentage, cutoffAdjPvalue=0.05, countFilter=1000)
peaks.gr <- unlist(GRangesList(peaks))
write.csv(as.data.frame(unname(peaks.gr)), "peaklist.csv", row.names=FALSE)

workflows.name: replicated_nad_seq
workflows.intent: Identify nucleolar-associated domains (NADs) from nucleolus-associated DNA and genomic DNA sequencing samples with multiple biological replicates.
input: nucleolus_rep1.bam, nucleolus_rep2.bam, nucleolus_rep3.bam (BAM files of replicated nucleolus-associated DNA)
genomic_rep1.bam, genomic_rep2.bam, genomic_rep3.bam (BAM files of replicated genomic DNA background)
workflows.stages: 1. Calculate read coverage in sliding windows using tileCount ;; 2. Compute log2 ratios of nucleolus vs genomic DNA across replicates using log2se ;; 3. Smooth ratios per chromosome using smoothRatiosByChromosome ;; 4. Assess quality using cumulativePercentage ;; 5. Call peaks using callPeaks (which utilizes limma for statistical significance across replicates) ;; 6. Visualize peaks along the ideogram using plotSig
workflows.code:
se <- tileCount(reads=file.path(path, f), genome=Mmusculus, windowSize=ws, step=step)
se <- log2se(se, nucleolusCols = c("N18.subsampled.srt-2.bam", "N18.subsampled.srt-3.bam", "N18.subsampled.srt.bam" ), genomeCols = c("G18.subsampled.srt-2.bam", "G18.subsampled.srt-3.bam", "G18.subsampled.srt.bam"), transformation = "log2CPMRatio")
seList<- smoothRatiosByChromosome(se, chr="chr18")
cumulativePercentage(seList[["chr18"]])
peaks <- lapply(seList, callPeaks, cutoffAdjPvalue=0.05, countFilter=1)
peaks <- unlist(GRangesList(peaks))
plotSig(ideo=ideo, grList=GRangesList(peaks), mcolName="AveSig", layout=list("chr18"), parameterList=list(types="heatmap"))
